entities.summary: Arnaud de Via was a French cardinal in the Roman Catholic Church. Born around 1290, he rose through the ranks of the Church, becoming a papal legate and a key advisor to Pope John XXII. De Via's influence extended beyond the ecclesiastical sphere, as he played a significant role in the politics of Western Europe during the 14th century. His brother Jacques, also a cardinal, and their mother, the sister of Pope John XXII, further underscored the family's prominent position within the Church. De Via's legacy is marked by his contributions to the development of the Catholic Church's diplomatic corps and his efforts to promote the interests of the French monarchy. His tenure as a cardinal came to an end in 1335, when he died on December 2nd of that year. De Via's life and career serve as a testament to the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized the medieval Church and the royal courts of Western Europe.
